TVS iQube battery instantly "failed" right after a routine tyre change service. Service centre demanding I pay for a replacement. Need advice!
Hey everyone, looking for some advice or to see if anyone else has faced this.

My dad rides a **TVS iQube** (purchased June 2023). It’s got **less than 30,000 km** on it, and he only uses it for short, gentle trips around the neighborhood at around 30 km/h. The scooter has been absolutely flawless—zero range drop, zero error codes. The night before taking it in, it was sitting happily at a **97% charge**.

On **16/09/2026**, I took it to an authorised service centre (**TVS RASSEE KARAIKUDI**) for a simple, routine tyre change and general service. The job card had absolutely no battery complaints listed.

**The Issue:**

The second I picked up the scooter post-service and started driving home, a **battery warning symbol started flashing** on the dashboard. I took it back the next morning. They ran a diagnostic check and immediately told me the battery pack had failed and I needed a total replacement out-of-pocket.

**Why I’m fighting this:**

**Timing:** It is technically and statistically impossible for a healthy battery to just "spontaneously die" the exact hour it's in a workshop for a tyre change. It feels highly likely that a technician messed up a firmware update, shorted something, or didn't reconnect the battery/sensors properly.

**Warranty:** The scooter is only about 2.5 months past its 3-year factory warranty, but *well* under the 30,000 km limit. TVS literally advertises that these batteries are built to last the lifetime of the vehicle.

I’ve already fired off a formal, legal-sounding complaint letter demanding diagnostic reports, cell voltage readings, log files, and a no-cost goodwill replacement.

**My questions for the community:**

Has anyone else had a TVS iQube battery warning trigger specifically after a workshop service? Is there a known firmware bug or sensor reset issue?

What are my chances of getting TVS to approve a corporate goodwill replacement since it’s only barely past the 3-year mark?

If they dig their heels in, what’s the best way to escalate this in India? Consumer Court (NCDRC) or standard grievance channels?

**TL;DR:** Took a perfectly running TVS iQube with 97% battery for a routine tyre change. Got it back with a flashing battery error. Service centre says the battery randomly died and wants me to pay for a new one.
